positives.subject: The five reserved stub members and their cost on workspace-wide jobs
positives.why: Examined and sanctioned, recorded here so the lens is on record as having checked it rather than raising it: the stubs are ratified reserved seams, so their per-crate compile unit on each job that builds the whole workspace is a sanctioned cost and not debt, and a performance entry about a reserved crate could only ever be about workspace cost, never about removing it. The cost is bounded to crate-level metadata for sources of a handful of lines each, so it is not worth a pointer.

positives.subject: Every MPICH source build is guarded by its own cache-hit condition
positives.why: Correct and worth protecting, and it is the reason every entry above is framed as a cache-miss cost: each Build step carries `if: steps.mpich-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'` (ci.yml:317 and its seven siblings), so on a warm key nothing is compiled and only the restore remains. A pointer that ignored this guard would be overstating the cost, and the perf epic should inherit the framing rather than re-derive it.

_needsHuman: Whether the MPICH prelude should stay uniform across every ci.yml job for readability even where the job's feature set does not demand it, or be derived per job from that feature set, is a workflow-style decision the owner owns; both MPICH entries above are written to be actionable either way.

Whether introducing a populator job and dependency edges for the shared MPICH key is worth serializing the workflow behind one job on a warm key is an owner trade-off, since today every consumer restores in parallel and nothing waits.

Whether the release cobre binary should have one producer and be passed between jobs, at the cost of losing the independence that stops one job's broken build from masking another's, is the owner's call between the two shapes named in that entry.

Whether the license tool's exact version pin and its feature selection are available as a prebuilt distribution is an external fact this read-only station cannot check at the baseline, and it decides whether that one call site can join the install-action amend.
